value.rationale: Single-center UK study with 100 patient target over 6-12 months. Standard recruitment for robotic prostatectomy trials typically achievable. Expected 90% recruitment based on typical trial completion rates.

value.uncertainty: Both insufflation systems have established safety profiles; adverse events expected to be documented per protocol
value.rationale: Both AirSeal and Stryker PneumoClear are established CE-marked devices. Expected safety profiles comparable to standard robotic prostatectomy. Adverse event documentation required by protocol will be completed.

value.uncertainty: Standard preoperative assessment; near-complete data capture expected

value.uncertainty: Standard preoperative labs; near-complete capture expected
value.rationale: Preoperative FBC, U&E, CRP, PSA are standard for prostatectomy patients. Complete data capture expected.

value.uncertainty: Study targets 8mmHg; some patients may require pressure increase
value.rationale: Study protocol specifies 8mmHg target pressure. AirSeal system maintains stable low pressure. Stryker may require occasional pressure increases. Expected mean near 8mmHg with some variation.

value.uncertainty: EBL typically 100-300ml for robotic prostatectomy; low pressure may reduce bleeding slightly
value.rationale: Robotic prostatectomy typically has EBL 100-300ml. Low pressure pneumoperitoneum may reduce venous bleeding slightly. Expected mean around 150ml for both groups.

value.uncertainty: Transfusion rare in robotic prostatectomy; expected <5% in both groups
value.rationale: Blood transfusion rarely needed in robotic prostatectomy. Expected rate <5% in both groups, likely 0-2%.

value.estimand: procedure time from incision to closure
value.uncertainty: Robotic prostatectomy typically 150-240 minutes; low pressure may add slight time initially
value.rationale: Robotic prostatectomy typically takes 150-240 minutes. Low pressure technique may initially add time but experienced surgeons maintain efficiency. Expected mean around 180 minutes.

value.estimand: need to increase IAP beyond study pressure
value.uncertainty: AirSeal valveless system may maintain pressure better; Stryker may require more frequent increases
value.rationale: AirSeal valveless trocar system maintains stable pneumoperitoneum. Stryker conventional insufflator may require more frequent pressure increases at 8mmHg. Expected 20% vs 40% need for increase.

value.uncertainty: TAP block use varies by institutional practice; expected 30-70% utilization
value.rationale: TAP block use depends on institutional protocol and anesthesiologist preference. Expected similar rates in both groups around 50%.

value.uncertainty: Low pressure may reduce intraoperative analgesia requirement; expected lower MME in AirSeal group
value.rationale: Low pressure pneumoperitoneum may reduce intraoperative pain. Expected lower morphine equivalent in AirSeal group (8mg) vs Stryker (12mg).

value.estimand: intraoperative pain score via MedaSense PMD-200
value.uncertainty: NOL index novel measure; expected lower scores with low pressure pneumoperitoneum
value.rationale: MedaSense PMD-200 NOL index measures nociception. Low pressure expected to reduce intraoperative pain. Expected AirSeal 20 vs Stryker 30.

value.uncertainty: Low pressure pneumoperitoneum reduces airway pressures; expected lower PAP in AirSeal group
value.rationale: Low intra-abdominal pressure reduces diaphragmatic compression and airway pressures. Expected PAP 18cmH2O AirSeal vs 22cmH2O Stryker.

value.uncertainty: Low pressure may slightly reduce CO2 absorption; expected similar ETCO2 between groups
value.rationale: Low pressure pneumoperitoneum may reduce CO2 absorption. Expected similar ETCO2 with slight trend lower in AirSeal group.

value.uncertainty: Low pressure may facilitate faster recovery; expected shorter time in AirSeal group
value.rationale: Reduced pain and physiological stress with low pressure may shorten recovery. Expected 110min AirSeal vs 130min Stryker.

value.rationale: Systematic reviews show low pressure reduces postoperative pain. Expected VAS 2.5 AirSeal vs 3.5 Stryker at 24 hours, converging by day 7.

value.uncertainty: Lower pain expected with AirSeal should reduce analgesia consumption
value.rationale: Reduced postoperative pain with low pressure should decrease analgesia requirements. Expected 25mg MME AirSeal vs 35mg Stryker.

analysis_trace.trial_identification: NCT06915909 RALP Trial - randomized controlled study comparing AirSeal Insufflation System vs Stryker PneumoClear insufflator for robotic prostatectomy at 8mmHg pneumoperitoneum pressure
analysis_trace.indication: Prostate cancer requiring robotic-assisted laparoscopic prostatectomy
analysis_trace.patient_population: Males aged 18-75 years, ASA Class I-III, undergoing non-emergent robotic prostatectomy
analysis_trace.target_mechanism: Low pressure pneumoperitoneum (8mmHg) with valveless trocar system (AirSeal) vs standard insufflator (Stryker PneumoClear) to reduce intraoperative and postoperative pain
analysis_trace.endpoint_interpretation: 26 primary endpoints covering recruitment, safety, perioperative measures, pain outcomes, and postoperative complications. No formal efficacy hypothesis specified - primarily descriptive/safety study
analysis_trace.safety_analysis: Low pressure pneumoperitoneum generally safe. AirSeal system allows stable insufflation at lower pressures. Expected adverse event rates comparable to standard robotic prostatectomy
analysis_trace.key_risks: 1) Recruitment challenges for single-center study 2) Surgeon learning curve with low pressure technique 3) Need to increase pressure intraoperatively in some patients 4) Pain measurement variability
analysis_trace.evidence_to_prediction: Based on systematic reviews of low pressure pneumoperitoneum in robotic urologic surgery showing reduced postoperative pain. AirSeal meta-analyses demonstrate comparable safety. No direct comparative evidence for Stryker PneumoClear at 8mmHg
analysis_trace.coverage_gaps: No published results for this specific trial. No direct head-to-head comparison of AirSeal vs Stryker PneumoClear at identical pressures. Limited data on Stryker device at ultra-low pressures

analysis_trace.indication: Prostate cancer requiring robotic-assisted laparoscopic prostatectomy
analysis_trace.patient_population: Males aged 18-75 years, ASA Class I-III, undergoing non-emergent robotic prostatectomy
analysis_trace.target_mechanism: Low pressure pneumoperitoneum (8mmHg) with valveless trocar system (AirSeal) vs standard insufflator (Stryker PneumoClear) to reduce intraoperative and postoperative pain
analysis_trace.endpoint_interpretation: 26 primary endpoints covering recruitment, safety, perioperative measures, pain outcomes, and postoperative complications. No formal efficacy hypothesis specified - primarily descriptive/safety study
analysis_trace.safety_analysis: Low pressure pneumoperitoneum generally safe. AirSeal system allows stable insufflation at lower pressures. Expected adverse event rates comparable to standard robotic prostatectomy
analysis_trace.key_risks: 1) Recruitment challenges for single-center study 2) Surgeon learning curve with low pressure technique 3) Need to increase pressure intraoperatively in some patients 4) Pain measurement variability
analysis_trace.evidence_to_prediction: Based on systematic reviews of low pressure pneumoperitoneum in robotic urologic surgery showing reduced postoperative pain. AirSeal meta-analyses demonstrate comparable safety. No direct comparative evidence for Stryker PneumoClear at 8mmHg
analysis_trace.coverage_gaps: No published results for this specific trial. No direct head-to-head comparison of AirSeal vs Stryker PneumoClear at identical pressures. Limited data on Stryker device at ultra-low pressures

analysis_trace: Trial NCT06915909 is a prospective, randomized, controlled, open-label study comparing AirSeal Insufflation System vs Stryker PneumoClear insufflator for robotic prostatectomy at 8 mmHg pneumoperitoneum pressure. Primary completion date is 2025-12-17 per protocol. Status is RECRUITING. Evidence search returned Europe PMC article MED/42164111 dated 2026-05-18 (post-cutoff, not usable for outcome data). No direct outcome results available pre-cutoff. Using indirect evidence from similar robotic prostatectomy trials and insufflation system comparisons. Evidence role: indirect_direction for most endpoints. Mismatch: articles are post-cutoff or different devices/populations. Numeric use not allowed for precise values. Baseline characteristics (vitals, BMI, labs) expected to be balanced by randomization. Perioperative outcomes (blood loss, procedure time) based on typical robotic prostatectomy ranges. Pain outcomes uncertain due to novel AI monitoring device. Safety outcomes expected low incidence based on standard robotic prostatectomy profile. Major uncertainty: no direct results available pre-cutoff; trial still recruiting; specific effect of Stryker PneumoClear vs AirSeal on pain is investigational. Confidence lowered accordingly.

Endpoint primary-0 (Recruitment rates): Descriptive measure, no directional hypothesis specified. Predict completion of estimated 100 patients over 6-12 months based on typical single-center recruitment rates.

Endpoint primary-1 (Adverse events): Safety monitoring endpoint. Expected low rates of serious adverse events for both devices based on standard robotic prostatectomy safety profile and published insufflation system meta-analyses showing comparable safety.
Endpoint primary-2 (Pre-op vitals): Baseline descriptive measure. Expected normal ranges for ASA I-III patients undergoing robotic prostatectomy. Randomization ensures balance between groups.
Endpoint primary-3 (Pre-op BMI): Baseline descriptive measure. Typical robotic prostatectomy population BMI ranges 25-30 kg/m². Randomization ensures balance.
Endpoint primary-4 (Pre-op labs): Baseline descriptive measure. Expected normal preoperative labs for selected patients (exclusion of significant comorbidities).

Endpoint primary-5 (Insufflation Pressure): Target 8 mmHg per protocol for both groups. Expected mean ~8 mmHg with minimal variation. Primary purpose is maintaining low pressure, not comparing different pressures.
Endpoint primary-6 (Estimated blood loss): Typical robotic prostatectomy EBL 150-400 mL. Low pressure pneumoperitoneum may reduce venous bleeding slightly. Expected similar between groups.
Endpoint primary-7 (Blood transfusion): Low incidence in robotic prostatectomy (<5%). Expected similar between groups, potentially slightly lower with stable pneumoperitoneum.
Endpoint primary-8 (Procedure time): Typical robotic prostatectomy 120-240 minutes. Insufflation system unlikely to significantly impact operative time at experienced center.

Endpoint primary-9 (Need to increase IAP): Key efficacy measure for insufflation stability. Valveless AirSeal may show lower need to increase pressure vs conventional. Uncertain for Stryker PneumoClear comparison.
Endpoint primary-10 (TAP block): Standard anesthetic technique. Expected high utilization (>80%) per institutional protocol, similar between groups.

Endpoint primary-11 (Intra-op analgesia): Measured in MME. Expected 10-30 MME typical. Lower pressure may reduce nociception; AI-guided monitoring may optimize dosing. Uncertain between-group difference.
Endpoint primary-12 (NOL pain score): Novel AI-based measure. No established normative data. Expected intraoperative values 10-40 range. Primary interest is between-group comparison.
Endpoint primary-13 (Peak Airway Pressure): Low pressure pneumoperitoneum (8 mmHg) expected PAP 15-25 cmH2O, lower than standard 12 mmHg. Similar between groups if pressure maintained.
Endpoint primary-14 (ETCO2): Expected 35-45 mmHg with 8 mmHg pneumoperitoneum. CO2 absorption may differ by insufflation system but clinically similar.
Endpoint primary-15 (Recovery room time): Typical 60-180 minutes. Enhanced recovery protocols may shorten. Insufflation system effect uncertain.
Endpoint primary-16 (Post-op pain): Primary interest endpoint. Low pressure may reduce shoulder pain, abdominal discomfort. VAS/NRS expected 2-4 at 24h. Between-group difference uncertain.
Endpoint primary-17 (Post-op analgesia): MME consumption 24-48h post-op. Expected 30-60 MME. May correlate with pain scores.
Endpoint primary-18 (Post-op labs): Expected transient changes (WBC elevation, CRP rise) typical post-surgery. No between-group difference expected.
Endpoint primary-19 (Vital signs 24hr): Expected stable vitals post-robotic prostatectomy. Low pressure may reduce hemodynamic perturbation slightly.
Endpoint primary-20 (PONV): Incidence 20-40% post-prostatectomy. Multimodal antiemetic protocols standard. No clear between-group difference expected.
Endpoint primary-21 (Hospital stay): Typical 1-3 days for robotic prostatectomy. Enhanced recovery may achieve same-day/23-hour discharge. Insufflation system effect uncertain.
Endpoint primary-22 (Complications Clavien-Dindo): Expected low grade I-II complications 10-20%. Major complications (≥III) <5%. No expected difference between devices.
Endpoint primary-23 (Return to OR): Rare event <2% in robotic prostatectomy. Bleeding, anastomotic leak typical causes. No expected difference.
Endpoint primary-24 (Readmission 30-day): Typical 5-10% for robotic prostatectomy. Urinary retention, infection, anastomotic issues common. No expected device-related difference.
Endpoint primary-25 (All AEs CTCAE v5.0): Comprehensive safety capture. Expected similar profile between groups based on mechanism of action similarity.
